"Not running x86 software" is a nicer way of saying "couldn't really do anything." I honestly think that the market was ready for a device like the Surface RT, but it was incapable of doing anything at launch, and it was not well-supported moving forward. Microsoft needed one of 3 things: * a translation layer with strong compatibility and performant emulation of x86 code * developers to port their apps to Windows RT * developers to create bespoke apps for Windows RT/tablet's and none of them really ever happened. It didn't help that the Surface RT (hence Windows RT) looked like the little brother variant of the Surface Pro. It would take Windows on ARM chip makers another decade before they were even feasible for a flagship PC.

It’s a great TV. I have one in my living room (not sure if it’s an F, but S95 from last year). But, my primary use is on my desk, I have 2 55” TVs as my monitors, and I’m not very comfortable with using OLEDs there. They can be on for basically the entire day with a lot of static images. RGB mini LED works better as I don’t have to worry about burn in, and TBH I like the image more than S95. It’s brighter with more intense colors (but without over saturation like Samsung tends to do). It’s still an LED backlight, so black won’t be as perfect as on OLED, but much better than QN95-whatever that I had before (that one was had an IPS panel, so off-axis glow was pretty bad), and it’s not noticeable unless it’s like a small text in black background. The only problem is size, 65” is too big (very immersive for games/movies/calls, but not great for work), but that’s just for my scenario. Hopefully they’ll shrink the tech for next generation.

I don't think it's necessarily strange for people to not like this approach to data management and as I mentioned in my post, there is a way for you to have your cake and eat it too with other software. It's a personal preference to want your data structure and the indexing of it to be separate. And there are ways to watch files and update the database as they are modified. It's not a "complaint" as much as just dissatisfaction with the way it currently works and for those that feel that way, they look to find other tools to do the job the way they want it to. Furthermore, by providing feedback to the Immich team, they quickly rolled out storage templates as the default, which is a net positive change I believe, so highlighting this stuff does have a purpose beyond just yelling into the internet void. Letting developers know what's important to you can help shape the project.
